deep.reconstruction:
OVERVIEW. This is routine practical astronomy: star places from old zone catalogues are reduced to new epochs. Two jobs appear. (A) A star near RA 164 deg, Dec +52 deg ("219 Bode" on fol. 280) is derived differentially from Lalande's zone of 1790 Feb 19/21, using 15 and 25 Ursae Majoris as reference stars, and carried to 1815.44. (B) Lalande's zone of 1794 March 25 is reduced to 1815 June 30, using Cor Caroli and 17 Canum as reference stars. The goal is presumably to get comparison stars for minor-planet observations of 1815; the planet is not named here (unsure). Angles written a.b.c mean a deg b' c". Sun and node longitudes are in signs (11.2.36 = 11 signs 2 deg 36' = 332 deg 36'). A trailing 'n' marks a negative logarithm.

I. Gauss's aberration-nutation scheme (verified numerically; the derivation is mine).
Notation: kappa = 20.25" (aberration constant), sun longitude L (Gauss's Theta), obliquity eps.
- Define A and Theta' by A cos Theta' = kappa cos L cos eps and A sin Theta' = kappa sin L. Gauss writes log A with sign n, i.e. A = -|A|.
- Aberration in RA: d_alpha = A cos(alpha - Theta') sec delta.
- Aberration in Dec: d_delta = A sin(Theta' - alpha) sin delta + (a cos(delta) term).
  - The cos(delta) term equals -kappa cos L sin eps cos delta.
  - Gauss writes it as two bracketed parts; I cannot determine how he splits it.
- Nutation: B sin(Omega') = d_psi sin eps and B cos(Omega') = -d_eps, again with B negative.
  - Nutation in RA: d_psi cos eps (the equation of the equinoxes, the same for every star) + B cos(alpha - Omega') tan delta.
  - Nutation in Dec: B sin(Omega' - alpha).
- Layout of the log blocks:
  - Row 1: logA, logA, logB, logB.
  - Row 2: log cos(alpha - Theta'), log sin(Theta' - alpha), log cos(alpha - Omega'), log sin(Omega' - alpha).
  - Row 3: log sec delta, log sin delta, log tan delta.
  - Row 4: the sums.

I.1 Epoch 1790 Feb.
- L = 332 deg 36', so A = 18.95, log 1.2775n. Theta' = 330 deg 32'.
- Node Omega = 7s 13 deg 50' (the marginal -2.4 is a small correction, unclear).
- Nutation: log B = 0.9322n, Omega' = 215 deg 33.5'.
- Equation of equinoxes +11.45".
- The implied coefficients are about 18.0" (longitude) and 9.65" (obliquity).

I.2 15 UMa.
- Catalogue place (1800): alpha = 133 deg 40'9.00", annual precession +64.89"; delta = 52 deg 24'0.50", annual -13.84".
- Carried back about 9.87 yr to 1790.13 (-10'39.89", +2'16.48"): mean place 133.29.29.11, 52.26.16.98.
- Corrections:
  - RA: aberration +29.71 (10^1.4729), equation of equinoxes +11.45, nutation -1.54 (10^0.1861n).
  - Dec: aberration +4.40 (10^0.6436), bracket -3.66 -0.71 (sum -4.37, equal to -kappa cos L sin eps cos delta = -4.36), nutation -8.47 (10^0.9280n).
- Apparent place: 133.30.8.73, 52.26.8.54.
- Add the zone differences 219-15 from fol. 280: 2h3m4.56s = +30 deg 46'8.40", and +4'22.50" in Dec.
- Result: 164.16.17.13, 52.30.31.04.

I.3 25 UMa.
- Catalogue place 139.50.52.80 (+61.15/yr), 52.34.45.40 (-15.94/yr).
- Carried back (-10'3.01", +2'37.19"): 139.40.49.79, 52.37.22.59.
- Corrections: RA +30.65 +11.45 -2.73; Dec +2.83 -3.65 -0.70 -8.30.
- Apparent place: 139.41.29.16, 52.37.12.77.
- Add 1h38m19.71s = +24 deg 34'55.65" and -6'45.00".
- Result: 164.16.24.81, 52.30.27.77.
- Margin 1s22 deg 26', 1s22 deg 37', mean 1s22 deg 30.5' = the declinations in sign notation.

I.4 The 164 deg star.
- Mean of the two derivations: 164.16.20.97, 52.30.29.40.
- Remove its own 1790 apparent corrections:
  - RA: aberration 30.23, equation of equinoxes 11.45, nutation -6.97.
  - Dec: aberration -3.57, bracket -3.66 -0.71, nutation -6.67.
- Mean place 1790.13: 164.15.46.26, 52.30.44.01.

I.5 Precession over t = 25.307 yr (logs in margin).
- log t = 1.40324, log m = 1.66313 (m = 46.04"), log n = 1.30241 (n = 20.06"), log nt = 2.70565.
- Then log cos alpha_m ~ 9.9838n, log sin alpha_m ~ 9.428, log tan delta_m = 0.11414, with mid-epoch alpha_m ~ 164 deg 27', delta_m ~ 52 deg 27'.
- RA: m t = +19'25.11" and n t sin alpha_m tan delta_m = +2'57.04".
- Dec: n t cos alpha_m = -8'9.17".
- Mean place 1815.44: 164.38.8.41, 52.22.34.84.

I.6 Apparent place, 1815 June.
- L = 2s 20 deg 59', Omega = 3s 4 deg 32'.
- Theta' = 81 deg 43', log A = 1.3057n; Omega' = 96 deg 5', log B = 0.8574n.
- Corrections:
  - RA: aberration -4.08, equation of equinoxes -16.49, nutation -3.42.
  - Dec: aberration +15.89, bracket +2.77 -3.54 (sum -0.77 = -kappa cos L sin eps cos delta), nutation +6.70.
- Apparent place: 164.37.44.42, 52.22.56.66.

II. Zone 1794 Mar 25 reduced to 1815 Jun 30 (epochs 1794.230 and 1815.496).

II.1 Reference star Cor Caroli.
- Catalogue place 191.39.42.30, +39.24.5.00.
- Carried back 5.77 yr (-4'4.76", +1'53.15"): 191.35.37.54, +39.25.58.15.
- 1794 Mar 25 values: L = 0s 5 deg 32', Omega = 4s 24 deg 50'.
  - Theta' = 6 deg 2', log A = 1.2694n; Omega' = 152 deg 19', log B = 0.9497n.
- Corrections:
  - RA: +23.96 aberration, -9.53 equation of equinoxes, -5.67 nutation.
  - Dec: -1.15, bracket -2.85 -3.34 (= -6.19 = -kappa cos L sin eps cos delta), +5.64.
- Apparent place: 191.35.46.30 = 12h46m23.09s, delta = 39.25.56.45.
- 17 Canum is done the same way on fol. 282: 13h0m35.22s, 39.35.46.50.

II.2 Zone reduction.
- Column 1: clock times. Column 2: zenith distances.
- Refraction:
  - Table values 9.20" at 9 deg and 10.30" at 10 deg.
  - Meteorological factor: thermometer 11.5 deg, log 9.9918; barometer 28 in 3 lines, log 0.0027; total log 9.9955.
  - Result: 9.11" at 9 deg and 10.19" at 10 deg, interpolated to +9.53, +9.49, +9.56, +9.38.
- Column 3: clock + about 35.5s = RA.
  - Comparison with Cor Caroli and 17 Canum leaves residuals -0.07 and +0.24.
  - The mean, +0.08s, is added to the two 8th-magnitude stars: 12h14m43.89s and 12h15m14.90s.
- Declinations: delta + z for the references gives 48.50.55.01 and 48.50.58.88, mean 48.50.56.94.
  - This is the Paris latitude plus the instrument index.
  - Subtracting the corrected z gives the two stars' 1794 apparent declinations: 39.27.27.41 and 39.29.24.45.
  - Fol. 282 continues to the 1815 mean places.
errors: In the Cor Caroli declination the listed corrections only give the written result 39.25.56.45 if the bracket term is -2.85, not -2.89 as transcribed. With -2.89 the result would be 56.41. The image most likely reads -2.85, so there is no error by Gauss.

Small sign-convention point: in the 164 deg star's 1790 block, log sin(Theta'-alpha) is written 9.3755 without 'n', yet the sum is marked 0.5523n. Since Theta'-alpha = 166.3 deg, the sine is positive and the negative sum comes from log A being n; so it is consistent.

No arithmetic errors found. All aberration, nutation and precession terms checked agree with the stated constants to about 0.01" (the 1815 log B is 0.8574 against my 0.8568, within the precision of the constants).

results.what: Reduction of mean to apparent place in the auxiliary-angle form. Aberration is A cos(alpha-Theta') sec delta in RA and A sin(Theta'-alpha) sin delta plus a cos(delta) term in Dec. Nutation is d_psi cos eps + B cos(alpha-Omega') tan delta in RA and B sin(Omega'-alpha) in Dec.
results.modern_name: Day-number / star-constant reduction for annual aberration and nutation (precursor of Bessel's A,B,C,D and a,b,c,d)
results.usually_credited_to: Classical (Bradley, Lacaille, Delambre); the systematic day-number form is Bessel, Tabulae Regiomontanae 1830; Gauss published aberration/nutation tables in Zach's Monatliche Correspondenz (c. 1808)

results.what: Precession over 25.3 years with m = 46.04", n = 20.06", using mid-epoch values of alpha and delta.
results.modern_name: Annual precession in RA/Dec (m + n sin alpha tan delta, n cos alpha)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard 18th-century practice; constants close to Bessel's

results.what: Differential re-reduction of Lalande zone observations. The clock correction and instrument constant come from reference stars, with refraction corrected for barometer and thermometer.
results.usually_credited_to: Standard; systematic reduction of Lalande's zones by Bessel/Baily later

deep.surprise_reason: Routine working computation. Gauss is known to have used and published aberration/nutation tables and to have reduced Lalande zone stars for minor-planet comparison stars. Nothing non-standard here.
